source_note: Metasploitable2 is Rapid7's intentionally-vulnerable practice VM, built specifically to have well-documented, publicly known vulnerabilities. This list is compiled from its widely-published vulnerability documentation (Rapid7's own Metasploitable2 exploitability guide and the broader pentesting community's write-ups on it) -- nothing here is a secret or a new finding, it's the standard reference list used to validate scanners against this VM.

known_vulnerabilities.note: The well-known vsftpd 2.3.4 backdoor (malicious code inserted into the source tarball briefly in 2011). Version-based, so this is the best-case scenario for CVE-keyword detection.
The Samba 'usermap_script' command injection. Version-based, should be keyword-detectable.
Same underlying Samba vulnerability, reachable on both 139 and 445.
distcc daemon allows arbitrary command execution when exposed without access control. Version-based.

This is a supply-chain backdoor (a trojaned source tarball distributed for a period in 2009), not a version-based code vulnerability with a CVE tied to the banner version. A keyword/CPE scanner has no way to distinguish a backdoored 3.2.8.1 build from a clean one -- this is an intentional test case for a *structural* false negative, not a scanner bug.

'Vulnerable' here means an insecure default configuration (unauthenticated RMI registry allowing remote class loading), not a version-specific code flaw. No CVE to detect against -- another structural false negative by design.
Vulnerable via default/weak admin credentials on the Tomcat Manager app, not a code CVE. A credential-based finding, not something CVE-keyword lookup can ever catch.
Vulnerable via a trivially weak configured password, not a version CVE. Same structural-false-negative category as above.
